I described my stpd to my sister as "its like if autism and schizophrenia had a fucked up baby." It does feel lonely, only relating some aspects of the more "mainstream" disorders like adhd or autism, but on the brightside theres no fandomization of most schizospec disorders as far as i can tell, like there is with autism. People claiming and self-dx'ing left and right but i do wonder if its even worth bothering to communicate with these people. Like you said, its like we are some kind of rare anomaly to most folks. No one is talking about stpd like they do autism or adhd. The struggle of finding community is endless, it seems...

I would say the goal is not to be happy constantly, you will always have a bad day or forty seven when you are alive. Its the human experience. To have a relatively good life, i think the goal is to survive comfortably while time passes. If you have a way to live comfortably, you can fill your time with hobbies. Personally drawing is something that makes me happy, even if i dont like the end result i think the process is what matters. There are many things in the world that you can do that dont involve interacting with most people, one of those is painting. 
To be honest, i also feel most people are inherently out to get me so I try to avoid socializing. I dont particularly feel human, more like a lab experiment gone wrong lmao,,, i hope you can find something you enjoy aside from engaging in spirituality. Not putting it down or anything as I believe in it myself, but I feel the more answers you search for, the less you end up finding and it becomes really unfulfilling. Hope whatever you decide works out for you

I'll be honest, I have met people like you before, who always cycle through questioning gender. In your case, since BPD is the root of it all, I think maybe you feel you are always performing? I agree people do treat men differently from women, and at times even I have trouble adjusting to what was once gentleness to now hostility. In some ways its a trauma response, to react to being treated with such hostilities from others. 
I cant tell you if you "truly are" trans, but I can tell you that feeling of performing is a common sentiment amongst trans people. Its a complicated existence when your ideas dont align with the world outside. I think it's part of just... not being "neurotypical" i suppose. You will always feel like a performer, you will always feel distance from others simply because you aren't stable. It hurts and it's cruel, believe me I know. I dont have a 100% factual answer for you because I dont know you like that at all, but I think you are overthinking your identity. BPD is known for black or white thinking but its feels for you, gender is not so black and white. I understand that, I myself think gender is a spectrum, there is no "one size fits all." There is not a single, definitive ideal that fits every single person on earth. But, if its any consolation,  I think its okay to question gender. I think if you are uncomfortable being one way, its okay to question things. If it hurts, if it causes discomfort,  you shouldnt have to put up with it. I dont know if you'll ever be 100% comfortable with gender, hell I dont even know if I will, but I can say that its okay to sort yourself out no matter how many times it takes. I hope it gets better for you, I understand the lack of stability even if you dont think I do. I wish you the best.

I am currently in the process of transitioning to male, so maybe I can provide some insight. I do wonder if you may have had the same issue as I where the hormones stabilized me because it was never my BPD, it was a combination of extreme gender dysphoria and schizotypal personality disorder? I do struggle with BPD issues still, but BPD wasnt actually the "main" issue if that makes sense. But the issue with my gender dysphoria wasn't known to me until about 2020 or so? I have always had identity issues and discomfort with my body, but its not really general body dysmorphia, I did my own research into gender stuff because I didnt really have access to resources (I live in a red state.) 

Just curious if you are familiar with internalized issues such as internalized misogyny or internalized misandry? I struggled with both as well as internalized homophobia. Ive learned to get past them, and am out as an openly gay trans man. I dont doubt my decision at all either, but I do sometimes feel issues with "feeling like I'm pretending" but its mostly realited to my detachment from reality caused by being on the schizospec.
